note: Each route is a real Component 4 Question 6, drawn from the Principal Examiner's report for that year (Professional/Exemplar-Work/Analysis-Documents/C4-Examiner-Report-Extracts-2019-2025.md). A step is { focus, caption, note } — focus ids accumulate as the route advances, so the finished question is a lit path across the room. Captions teach the move; notes quote or tightly paraphrase the examiner.

routes.title: The vocal chain
routes.stem: A rock vocal through three processors — compression, EQ, then delay. Evaluate the settings.

steps.caption: First stop: a very high ratio means a heavily compressed vocal — say what that does.
steps.note: Examiner, 2023: the make-up gain's job was often confused and misunderstood.

steps.caption: The EQ boosts mids and highs, so the vocal brightens and comes forward in the mix.
steps.note: Examiner, 2023: very few noticed boosting the lows invites muddiness against the bass guitar.

steps.caption: High feedback means too many repeats; the delay time is tempo-synced at a quaver.
steps.note: Examiner, 2023: very few candidates worked out the quaver tempo-sync.

steps.caption: The two delay times differ on purpose — offset repeats build a stereo image.
steps.note: Examiner, 2023: some argued the offset was a mistake and would have removed it.

steps.caption: One question, four rooms. A subheading per processor produced the most concise, highest-scoring writing.
steps.note: Examiner, 2023: a lot of credit is given for a single, well-constructed sentence.

routes.title: The analogue synth pad
routes.stem: An old analogue synthesiser (a Juno-6). Extrapolate the synth-pad sound from its controls.

steps.caption: Name what you see first — oscillators, sub-oscillator, waveforms. Naming alone caps at five marks.
steps.note: Examiner, 2019: candidates who only listed parameters maxed out at 5 AO3 marks.

steps.caption: The discriminator: the envelope drives the filter cutoff here, not the volume.
steps.note: Examiner, 2019: only the top candidates noticed the envelope was routed to the filter.

steps.caption: The LFO is a control signal, not an audible bass note — a mark-losing confusion.
steps.note: Examiner, 2019: a surprising number thought the LFO was for audible bass.

steps.caption: Chorus on the pad earned marks when its effect on the sound was described, not named.
steps.note: Examiner, 2019: pulse width moved by the LFO adds movement — very few explained it.

steps.caption: A synthesis question that lives in three rooms — the marks sit in the connections.
steps.note: Examiner, 2019: understanding how the sections interact received a lot of credit.

routes.title: Bass pedals for funk
routes.stem: Four bass guitar pedals — overdrive, EQ, compression, wah. Evaluate them for a funk track.

steps.caption: Gain drives the clipping; level sets the output. Swapping them cost whole paragraphs.
steps.note: Examiner, 2022: the gain-versus-level confusion made a lot of writing uncreditable.

steps.caption: EQ was the best-answered pedal — describing how a boost muddies the bass earned marks.
steps.note: Examiner, 2022: EQ best answered, then overdrive, then compression, then wah.

steps.caption: Compression on bass evens the level and adds sustain — say why funk wants that.
steps.note: Examiner, 2022: many scored 8–12 — full AO3 plus only a few applied points.

steps.caption: The wah is a swept filter peak. Knowing how it worked unlocked the top band.
steps.note: Examiner, 2022: wah understanding gave access to another five or so marks.

steps.caption: Highest scorers evaluated how the pedals interact in the chain — order matters.
steps.note: Examiner, 2022: apply knowledge to the scenario; a page of generic revision scored one mark.

routes.title: Two guitars, one chain
routes.stem: EQ, gating and reverb across two differently treated guitars. Evaluate the settings in a mix.

steps.caption: Precision first: it is a parametric EQ — calling it a notch filter lost marks.
steps.note: Examiner, 2020: much incorrect terminology — parametric EQs called notch filters or BPFs.

steps.caption: Read settings against consequence: this gate threshold would silence the rhythm guitars entirely.
steps.note: Examiner, 2020: the gate would yield silence — only a few students noticed.

steps.caption: Routing is knowledge too — reverb placed as an insert changes what the chain does.
steps.note: Examiner, 2020: very few candidates commented on the routing at all.

steps.caption: The guitars are hard-panned, so the stereo picture is wide — the easiest applied mark.
steps.note: Examiner, 2020: noting the wide stereo picture was the easiest AO4 mark to score.

steps.caption: Four topics in one diagram. The best answers compared the two guitars' opposite settings.
steps.note: Examiner, 2020: state which guitar you mean — unattributed points could not be credited.
